coordinates.object_orientation: Head -Y, tail +Y, dorsal +Z. Keep fixed camera conventions.

concept.reason: Actual scaled specimen photographs plus published complete reconstruction cover shape; no new concept image necessary.

scope: Complete Carboniferous living scorpion, anchored to NMS G.1987.7.136 with missing appendages interpreted using Dunlop and Garwood 2024 Figure 9, third animal. Not a fossil slab or a modern scorpion substitute.

scientific_limits.en: Approximate dimensions estimated from the 10 cm bar of specimen NMS G.1987.7.136, not direct measurements or the popular giant maximum. The specimen is fragmented; symmetry, missing limbs, living depth, upward tail pose and color are inferred. Published genus reconstruction guides absent appendages.
scientific_limits.zh: 尺度由 NMS G.1987.7.136 标本照片的 10 厘米图尺估算，不是实测，也不采用网络巨型上限。标本有碎裂，左右对称、缺失附肢、活体厚度、上弯尾姿与颜色为推断；缺失部分参考公开同属复原。

scale.uncertainty: Approximate photo-bar estimates, about 15-20 percent; total excludes pedipalps and legs and measures tail centerline, not posed bounding box.

anatomy: Broad ribbed mesosoma with seven dorsal tergites; approximately rectangular carapace with anterior median eye prominence interpreted from target Figure 9. Do not copy lateral compound eyes of the second animal, Proscorpius.

A pair of small anterior chelicerae, one pair of long pedipalps ending in slender fingers and modest palms, and four pairs of walking legs. Walking legs progressively reach farther posteriorly; do not copy digitigrade tapering Palaeophonus legs.

Five distinct articulated metasomal segments followed by a separate bulbous telson with curved sting. Tail held gently upward in life interpretation, with rounded joints rather than fossil fragment gaps.
Pedipalp chela fingers long relative to small palm. Do not turn into short massive modern emperor scorpion pincers. Broad dorsum and long segmented tail preserve original visual gate.

Ventral coxae remain close to sternum as mesoscorpion group A described by Jeram; do not expose internal book lungs as external organs. Tiny uncertain ventral details simplified rather than fabricated.
restoration_boundaries: Actual NMS specimen is fragmented and appendages displaced. Fossil gaps and detached pincer are taphonomic, not live anatomical segmentation. No claim of complete single-specimen preservation.
NMS G.1987.7.136 is not asserted to be a holotype; official type-status field does not establish that. Visean, East Kirkton Quarry, Bed 47.
2024 Figure 9 third animal is a scholarly genus-level whole-animal interpretation, not the NMS specimen scan. Other three genera are excluded.
Original Jeram abstract accessed; full paywalled text not claimed read. PeerJ and PMC access blocked, no bypass; independently accessible attributed CC-BY Figure 9 was inspected.
Depth, leg joint pose, tail upcurve and muted brown coloration are interpretation. Do not infer exact color or eye-lens count from black diagram.
BGS photographs and scientific diagrams remain private research; no borrowed mesh or image texture in product.
quality_gates: Complete animal: small chelicerae, slender pedipalps, four walking-leg pairs, broad seven-tergite mesosoma, five tail segments and curved telson.
Compare primary real specimen for broad body and slender detached chela; compare only third animal of Fig.9 for absent paired limbs.
Tail must be long and gently upcurved, segmented rather than a smooth tube; no fossil fragmentation gaps.
Dimensions remain approximate specimen-photo estimates, not maximum 70 cm claim.
Four fixed views only. Reviewer inspect ventral joins directly; no extra default renders.
